title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
data_curation: Training data comes from Environment Scaling over three executable world families, all sharing one task contract E=(W, W0, q, A, T, Omega, B, D, V_D). File worlds are profession-conditioned multi-format workspaces built inverse-first from latent business state, drawn from a registry of 33 domains, 318 occupations and 1,208 deliverable clusters; graded quantities must be re-derivable by code or tied to recorded provenance. Search worlds supply gold source sets with claim-to-evidence alignment, and difficulty is set by acquisition pressure rho_acq=(N_cand+N_hop)/B_tool. Code worlds mix harvested PR environments (fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests) with synthesized ones expanded from verified seeds. Their verifiers are hardened first, and probed for reward-hacking attacks that succeed in the sandbox. A trajectory is kept only if it can be replayed (world seed, tool and verifier versions, file deltas). Coordination traces cover delegation, integration, replanning and 12+ kinds of user intervention. SFT filtering drops invalid tool calls, inconsistent state, ignored observations and incomplete delivery, using reject sampling against gold answers or per-dimension rubric thresholds.
curriculum: Post-training is unified SFT followed by agentic RL, inside a controlled capability-development loop. SFT variants are trained per major domain (general, agentic, coding) and model-soup merged into a single behavioral initialization for RL. RL then runs over environment and coordination trajectories. After each training round, failed trajectories, benchmark errors and runtime failures are abstracted into capability gaps. A Task Pipeline turns these gaps into new tasks and worlds, which re-enter family-specific verification, and expert and user feedback decide the next allocation of training effort. The authors call this 'self-evolution' but restrict it to this managed engineering loop. RL batches mix localized pivot continuations with unhinted full tasks. Pre-training and base-model details are not described.
method: Apodex 1.1 is a general-purpose model (397B per the HDS6 analysis; Apodex 1.1 mini is 35B) plus an execution system. RL uses PIVOT-RL. Hindsight analysis locates 'pivots', the decisions where a trajectory turns unproductive. Training keeps the useful prefix, restores the environment state, and adds a short corrective hint that is never a prediction target and is absent at inference. Optimization is asynchronous, so completed trajectories enter without waiting for slow episodes. Agentic Coordination Scaling trains a lead agent to write its decomposition to an external Task Board, spawn problem-induced subagents, and integrate staged asynchronous returns. It also covers absorbing mid-run user interventions without changing (q, D), asymmetric verification (narrow claim-level falsification instead of re-solving), and Adaptive Max Team Effort (extra fan-out only on contested, load-bearing claims). AgentOS 1.1 provides /inputs, /workspace and /outputs namespaces, a provenance graph, tiered compaction triggered by provider-reported tokens, soft/hard deadlines with bounded finalization, and a single-publisher lease with an exact output manifest. Hyperparameters are not reported.
eval_metrics: The paper evaluates two modes, ReAct (minimal scaffold) and Agent Team. Professional work: APEX-Agents (34.4 ReAct / 38.5 Team) and GDPVal win rate (69.5 / 78.8). Finance: FrontierFinance (48.7 / 54.3) and YC-Bench net worth ($1.04M ReAct). Science: FrontierScience-Research (55.0 / 63.3) and BioMysteryBench Human-difficult (23.5 / 35.3). Reasoning and search: HLE with tools (53.2 / 56.1) and DeepSearchQA F1 (88.2 / 92.4). Math (MathArena protocol, Agent Team): IMO 2025 36.5, IMO 2026 30.5, USAMO 2026 26.5, all above the reference thresholds of 35, 29 and 25; IMO-ProofBench Basic 96.7 / Advanced 63.3. Coding: Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.8 and SWE-bench Verified 77.7. Internal benchmarks: FrontierSearchBench (41 tasks, score in [-100,100]) 57.0 / 69.1; FrontierResearchBench pass rate 12.4% (Agent Team); and HDS6 process grading (6 capabilities x 4 items, judged by a GPT-5.5/Claude panel with an integrity gate). The 35B mini scores FrontierFinance 50.2, FrontierScience 51.7 and APEX-Agents 27.7 with Agent Team.
key_results: With Agent Team, Apodex 1.1 posts the best values in its comparison tables on FrontierFinance (54.3, vs Claude Fable 5 at 49.2) and FrontierScience-Research (63.3, vs DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at 55.0), and passes the IMO 2025/2026 and USAMO 2026 thresholds. On APEX-Agents it improves from Apodex 1.0's 16.5 to 38.5, and it reaches GDPVal 78.8. It still trails the frontier on SWE-bench Verified (77.7 vs Claude Opus 5's 92.2), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (70.8 vs 91.9) and FrontierResearchBench (12.4% vs 20.6%).
evolution_note: Apodex 1.1 extends Apodex 1.0's lead-agent/subagent Agent Team and AgentOS kernel. It follows the 2025-26 shift from single-response models to long-horizon working agents (Kimi K3, GPT-5.6, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4), and it treats environment construction (in the vein of ScaleEnv and Agent-World) and multi-agent coordination as two explicit scaling axes. PIVOT-RL's hinted continuation from failure pivots joins recent work on credit assignment at informative intermediate turns in agentic RL. The paper is light on model and training hyperparameters and heavy on harness and evaluation design, including process-level HDS6 grading.
